wps.title: Market packs: lessons that read local in German, French and Arabic markets

lenses.prompt: Lens: correctness and completeness against the brief. Does every acceptance item hold? Is the substitution deterministic and idempotent, guarded by the locale-parity checker, and does every substituted file still validate? Are the 'brands' analogues fictional (no real company names)? Edge cases: amounts and currency formats, grammatical cases in German, gender agreement in French and Arabic, RTL punctuation.

Lens: a native German reader and a native French reader. Open at least fifteen substituted lesson files per language and read them as an employee of a bank in Frankfurt / Paris would: do names, cities, authorities, courier/bank/tax/cloud analogues, currency and phone formats read local and natural? List every sentence that reads translated-from-Azerbaijan or breaks grammar after substitution, with file and sentence.

Lens: a native Arabic reader (Gulf and Levant). Open at least fifteen substituted Arabic lesson files and read them as an employee of a bank in Riyadh / Amman would: names, cities, authorities, analogues of banks, couriers, tax and government portals, currency and phone formats, RTL punctuation and digits. List every sentence that reads foreign, breaks grammar or mixes dialect inconsistently, with file and sentence.

wps.brief:
Strategic item 4.1 (owner item 1: the content lives in an Azerbaijani world; learners in other markets must see their own banks, couriers, authorities, cities, names and amounts). Read .claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/lesson-engine.md (lesson JSON, artifacts, brands), the glossaries under references/glossaries/, portal/content/library/brands.json (fictional brand registry) and a sample of de/fr/ar lesson files first. wave C added formatVersion 1 to every lesson file: keep it.
DESIGN: (1) portal/content/market/<lang>.json for de, fr and ar (schema in src/lib/content/market.ts, validated by zod): people names (given + family, gendered where the language needs it), cities and districts, currency code and formatting, typical amounts for each amount placeholder class (salary, invoice, fine, gift card), phone formats, government bodies (tax, police, courts, social insurance), and brand analogues per brand id in brands.json (fictional, locally plausible: a Sparkasse-like bank, a DHL-like courier, an Elster-like tax portal for de; La Poste/Colissimo-like, impots-like for fr; a Gulf bank, Aramex-like courier, government portal analogues for ar) with per-language `name`, `domain` (fictional TLD look-alikes stay fictional) and short description. (2) A substitution pass (portal/scripts/apply-market.ts): reads the localized lesson files of a language, replaces the Azerbaijani-world tokens (the person names, cities, 'Bakı', manat amounts, '+994' numbers, DövlətPortal-like brands, AZN) with the market pack's values, deterministic (seeded choice per lesson so the same character keeps the same name within a lesson), idempotent (a marker in the file or a reversible token map keeps re-runs stable), never touching scene ids, option ids, correct flags, or the English source; the result is committed as the lesson files themselves (no runtime cost). First survey the Azerbaijani-world tokens actually present in the de/fr/ar files (names, cities, brands, amounts, phone numbers) and put the list in the summary with counts. (3) The lesson-locale checker (scripts/check-lesson-locales.ts) gains a market check: a substituted language must not contain tokens from the Azerbaijani world list; all 954 translations still pass. (4) brands.json entries gain the optional per-language name map read by the artifact renderer (src/components/player artifacts, templates) so simulated e-mails/SMS show the local brand. (5) Run the pass for de, fr, ar; tr, ro, ka, uk and ru get a pack skeleton (empty values documented) and are left for the owner's reviewers (left_open). Tests: market schema validation, substitution determinism/idempotence on a fixture lesson, the checker's market rule, brand name resolution per language.
acceptance: de, fr and ar lesson files read local (names, cities, authorities, brand analogues, amounts, phones) with no Azerbaijani-world tokens left (checker rule + reader reviews)
Substitution is deterministic and idempotent and never changes scene/option ids or correctness (tests); 954/954 translations still pass the checker
Artifacts and templates show the per-language brand names (test)
typecheck, lint, content tests pass; left_open lists the languages left for native reviewers

wps.title: Teachable-moment loop: click → micro-lesson → re-simulation

lenses.prompt: Lens: integrity and isolation of the loop. The micro-lesson assignment, its completion evidence, the risk effect and the scheduled re-simulation must be organisation-scoped, idempotent under replays (a click recorded twice, a job tick run twice), impossible to trigger for another organisation's person, and unable to inflate or deflate XP/risk outside the rules of ADR-035. Every finding with file:line and a concrete scenario.

Lens: correctness and completeness against the brief. Does every acceptance item hold? Job timing, due dates in the organisation's time zone, ten-locale micro-lesson text, the offline fallback without an AI key, the admin loop view, settings toggle, tests that assert the behaviour.

wps.brief:
Strategic item 4.2 (owner item 2). Read the training pipeline reference (assignments, reminders, risk, behaviour risks), src/server/tracking.ts (recordClick/recordSubmit, wave B's beacon), src/server/jobs.ts, src/lib/campaigns/templates.ts (red flags per template) and the Studio lesson builder in src/server/actions/secops.ts first.
DESIGN: (1) Within the hour after a person's click or submit on a simulation (job step 'teachable', per organisation, hourly ledger from wave C), a 90-second micro-lesson is created for that campaign template if it does not exist yet: a lesson_contents row per organisation locale under a hidden library module 'teachable:<templateKey>' built from the template's red flags (intro beat, a choice with the template's own lure, a hotspot or swipe on the template artifact, recap) — text generated offline from the template texts in the ten message files (no AI dependency; an AI-polished variant only when aiEnabled, cached). (2) The micro-lesson is assigned to the person with a due date 7 days out (existing assignments/reminders machinery; organisation time zone), tagged as 'teachable' so the Home card shows the reason; completing it goes through the server-verified path (ADR-035) and closes the behaviour risk the click opened. (3) Two weeks after the micro-lesson is completed (or after 21 days if it is not), the job schedules a re-simulation for that person only: a one-person campaign of the same category at the next difficulty (templates have difficulty), launched through launchCampaign in the organisation's normal sending path (it respects providers; nothing is sent when mail is not configured — the campaign goes back to draft with the existing reason), linked to the original campaign in a new table teachable_loops (schema.ts only: id, tenant_id, user_id, source_campaign_id, source_recipient_id, micro_module_id, assigned_at, completed_at, resim_campaign_id, resim_result, status). (4) Settings → Learning gains 'Teachable moments' on/off per organisation (default on) with the two delays shown; ten locales. (5) Admin view: /admin/campaigns/[id] gains a 'Loop' section listing click → micro-lesson (assigned/completed) → re-simulation (scheduled/sent/result) per person; the leadership risk story (wave B) may cite the loop's success rate (optional). (6) Tests: a click creates one assignment (idempotent on replay), completion closes the risk, the re-simulation is scheduled on time in the organisation's zone and only once, another organisation's recipient is never touched, the toggle off creates nothing, the micro-lesson validates with the lesson schema in ten locales.
acceptance: A simulation click produces one micro-lesson assignment within the hour, in the person's language, through the server-verified completion path (tests, idempotent on replay)
A re-simulation of the same category and next difficulty is scheduled once per loop and only when the organisation can send (tests)
Administrators see the loop per person on the campaign page; the organisation can switch the loop off (ten locales)
typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; nothing under portal/drizzle committed

wps.title: A data-driven mini-lab for every module (English content; translation pipeline wired)
wps.brief:
Strategic item 4.4 (owner item 5). Read the VM lab engine (portal/src/components/lab/**, src/lib/domain/labs.ts LAB_IDS/labUnlocked/LAB_MODULES, the lab result actions and tests) and the lesson-engine reference first.
DESIGN: (1) A generic 'inbox moment' mini-lab in the VM lab engine driven by data: portal/content/library/labs/<module-slug>.en.json (schema in src/lib/content/lab-scenario.ts, validated like lessons, formatVersion 1) describes 3–5 decisions built from that module's own lesson artifacts (an e-mail, SMS, call note, file or browser tab from the module's scenes), each decision with options, the safe choice, a short debrief line and a risk tag; the engine renders it with the existing apps (MailApp, FilesApp, BrowserApp, TerminalApp) and the existing debrief; scoring is server-side through the existing lab result action (the browser sends chosen option ids only, as ADR-035 does for lessons). (2) Write the 53 English scenarios from the modules' lessons (read each module's lessons; reuse their artifacts and brands; no new real company names). (3) Catalog and paths: each module page lists its mini-lab after the lessons ('Practise' card), unlocked when the module's lessons are complete (labUnlocked), 10–15 XP, counted in module completion only as optional (does not block attestation); ten-locale UI strings. (4) Translation: the mini-lab files use the same translation pipeline as lessons: extend scripts/check-lesson-locales.ts (coverage counts labs separately), the translation workflow scripts under docs/build/workflows (the translator/editor process of ADR-026) accept the labs folder, and the player reads <slug>.<locale>.json with en fallback. Do NOT translate the 53 scenarios yourself (that runs as its own wave); say so in left_open. Tests: scenario schema, all 53 files validate, server scoring of a fixture scenario, unlock rule, catalog listing.
acceptance: 53 English mini-lab scenarios validate and render through the VM lab engine; scoring is server-side (tests)
Each module page offers its mini-lab after the lessons, unlocked by completion, with XP (tests)
The lesson translation pipeline and checker cover the labs folder (checker reports coverage for labs)
typecheck, lint, content and lab tests pass

wps.title: Narration clips in every browser: provider-agnostic generator, Piper for English now, Azure path for Azerbaijani and Russian
wps.brief:
Strategic item 4.7 (owner addition 2026-11-05; register M-04; OPEN-QUESTIONS 2). Read docs/build/NARRATION-RESEARCH.md (the decisions), the lesson-engine reference §3.4 and recipe 6.6, portal/scripts/generate-narration.ts, the manifest format, src/components/player narration hooks (useNarrator, clipKey) first. SCOPE NOW (owner): clips for az, en and ru only; the other seven languages keep the Web Speech default; the pipeline must support all ten so widening is one command.
DESIGN: (1) Provider abstraction in the generator: --provider elevenlabs|piper|azure, each returning PCM/WAV plus word timings when the provider gives them (Piper alignments, Azure word boundaries, ElevenLabs timestamps), else a proportional per-sentence estimate so karaoke still moves. (2) Piper provider: runs on the build machine only (GPL engine never ships): `py -3.12 -m pip install --user piper-tts` is ALLOWED for this package (say in the summary which version was installed), the en_US-ljspeech-high voice (public domain) downloaded into a git-ignored portal/.voices/ folder from the Piper voices repository with its checksum recorded; generate the English clips for all 106 lessons. (3) Encoding: MP3 mono 48 kbps with loudness normalisation through ffmpeg; ffmpeg is not installed on this machine — you may add the devDependency `ffmpeg-static` (exact version, used on the build machine only, never shipped) and run `npm install` in your worktree (node_modules is a junction to the main checkout: that is intended) and commit the updated package-lock.json; if that fails, keep WAV output and say so in left_open. Clips go to portal/public/narration/<lang>/<clipKey>.mp3 (git-ignored, served immutable), manifest per language committed. (4) Azure provider: full implementation against the Azure Speech REST API (SSML, az-AZ-BanuNeural/BabekNeural, ru-RU voices, word-boundary events via the synthesis metadata), tested with a fake HTTP server; requires AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION in .env.local — do not run it live; the exact owner ask goes to left_open (key, region, voice choice after listening to a sample). (5) Player: the narrator prefers a clip when the manifest has it, falls back to Web Speech otherwise (unchanged contract), unlocks audio on the first user gesture (iOS), preloads the next sentence's clip, hides the volume slider on iOS (volume is read-only there), shows a 'synthetic voice' note in the player's audio menu (ten locales), and uses exact word timings when present. (6) `npm run narration -- --lang en --provider piper` documented in portal/README.md and the skill reference; Dockerfile/CI do NOT generate clips yet (the owner decides where the build machine is: left_open). Tests: manifest shape, timing estimator, fallback order (clip → Web Speech), clipKey includes provider:voice, Azure provider against the fake server, player audio-unlock logic.
acceptance: English clips exist for every lesson sentence (manifest committed, clips git-ignored) and play through <audio> in the player with karaoke timings from Piper alignments
The Azure provider is implemented and tested against a fake server; the owner ask for az/ru is precise in left_open
Fallback order, audio unlock, prefetch, iOS volume handling and the synthetic-voice note work (tests + summary)
typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; new dependency and tool installs listed in the summary
